Hosea says the same: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”. Many days without a king. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

We are returning now. We are seeking the Lord our God. And it is telling you David is going to be alive in these last days, in the latter days, when Israel returns. That is the day of Jeremiah 30, when the yoke is broken off our neck and the Lord raises David up unto us.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:11
precepts.why:
If David is alive in these last days, “David their king, whom I will raise up unto them”, why doesn't anyone know it? Solomon says: “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.”

David will not remember who he is, and neither do you. Our minds are wiped, everybody. We don't know who's who. That is why it says love your neighbour as you love yourself: you don't know who is who.

And that is a good thing. In the old school we used to say, oh, this one's David, and that caused a lot of partiality and a lot of problems. Don't do that. Don't try to guess who anybody is either. Little brother calling himself Samson: you don't know, brother. Just stop it. The Lord will raise up David; it is not ours to name him.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 34:23
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Israel “shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Ezekiel says the same of the last days: “And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.”

One shepherd over the whole nation, and that shepherd is David. After Israel has abided many days without a king, the Lord himself sets David up over them, to feed them.

That is part of the promise that comes at the end of the exile and tribulation: the yoke broken from our neck, the strangers no longer serving themselves of us, Jacob returned to rest and quiet with none to make him afraid, and one shepherd, David, raised up over Israel under the Lord their God.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 9:22
precepts.why:
“though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee”. Why is he going to make an end of all nations? Ezra says it: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”.

All these nations were born in vain. In a movie they are the extras; they're not the stars of the movie. We are. And Esau is the villain, the antagonist, the bad guy.

But the stars are not spared from correction: “I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.” The Lord makes a full end of the nations, but only corrects Israel in measure. So “fear thou not, O my servant Jacob”. What he says will happen would make anyone afraid, and nobody wants to go through tribulation, so we increase our faith by reminding ourselves that this body is just a shell; the real us is within. He will save us from afar, and Jacob shall return and be in rest, and none shall make him afraid.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:12-17
thread.text: For thus saith the Lord, Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous.

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:4-6
precepts.why:
“Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.” None stands up on our behalf, and we have no healing medicine. Every Negro that just popped out of his mama's behind has a new idea for how to save black people, and it is always economics or voting. Those medicines don't work. What is the wound? Our sins. Isaiah says the same thing.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” We are that sinful nation, a people laden with sin; iniquity is sin. He calls us a seed of evildoers.

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”. Our people get punished and revolt more and more against God. Then: “the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint”: the whole head of the Israelites is sick.

“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Neither mollified with ointment means no medicine: there is no healing for us that way. That is Jeremiah's “no healing medicines.”

The only one who can save us is the Saviour, Jesus Christ, our master, our king. Yes, he is our rabbi, and rabbi means master. The wound Jeremiah calls incurable is incurable by any remedy of men; only the Lord can say, “I will restore health unto thee”.

precepts.label: Job 2:7
precepts.why:
What Isaiah and Jeremiah say of the nation is the same thing Job went through. People read Job and think that was only him, but Job's real life symbolizes the nation of Israel. This was the fifth judgment on Job: “So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” Didn't we just read that in Isaiah 1? “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it”.

Job's life is Deuteronomy 28. He lost his businesses, his family, everything. And “There is none to plead thy cause”: Job had friends who would not stand up on his behalf. They were always telling him he was wrong, evil, the devil. There was no cure; God had to intervene and heal Job. That is why the Lord sent Christ to heal the twelve tribes of Israel.

Even Job's wife turned on him in his darkest moment, when he had lost everything. That is how these black women do with us: in this state, the black woman turned on us.

But at the end of Job's life he was blessed. That is what is going to happen to us if we endure to the end: the incurable wound of Jeremiah 30 ends with “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”.

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:41
precepts.why:
“I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.” Our sins are increased: the Houston rodeo, black men and women whoring themselves out, filthy and wicked, so bad a dress code had to be put in place; and in Delta State in Nigeria, a festival where women are openly raped in the streets. That is evil. Then: “because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee”.

Moses said it would be so: “And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”. God walked contrary to us because we kept breaking his laws, and he brought us into the land of our enemies. Then what we must do: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”.

As we repent, we have to accept that God is right and we are wrong. We have always been wrong. God was just when he punished us. When your child plays in the street or with the light socket, you beat that behind, not because you hate him but so he learns he'll die playing in traffic or with electricity. Some talking doesn't do any good for some kids; you have to rile up on them so they know it's serious. That is what God did with us.

The three holy children did exactly this. In the midst of the fiery furnace, cast in because they would not worship Babylon's god, Azarias prayed: “Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers”, “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” Then: “for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins. For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee”. Everything God has done to our people is justified, because we revolted against him. They said it because of what Moses said in Leviticus, and what happened to them is a reflection of what will happen to us.

Christianity has taught our people the opposite: to mock a God who got angry at his own people for worshipping a golden calf. But accepting the punishment is the way back, because the next verse is: “Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob”.

precepts.label: Luke 9:11
precepts.why:
“For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. The Lord is the only one who can restore health; that goes back to verses 12 and 13, “thou hast no healing medicines.” There is no magic voting right and no economic situation to save us.

Luke shows who the healer is: “And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.” Christ spake of the kingdom and healed them that had need of healing. He is the only one who can heal us of all these things. He is the Saviour; he is the physician.

That is how the incurable bruise of Jeremiah 30 is cured. Not by any medicine of man, but by the Lord who received the people, taught them the kingdom of God, and healed them.

precepts.label: Mark 2:17
precepts.why:
Christ is the physician: “When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick”. If you think you're good, that you know everything, you don't need the son of God, you don't need the Saviour.

You have to admit you're sick: that we are in the midst of sin, and that all we have done has been wrong. That is the same thing as accepting the punishment of our iniquity.

“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” He did not call us righteous. He came for sinners. That is the healing Jeremiah promises Israel, whose “sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity”. The sick nation is the one he came to heal.

The churches are the opposite: they say they don't need that Bible, they are already whole. Isaiah 65 shows them saying so, “I am holier than thou.” The ones who think themselves whole will not come to the physician.

precepts.label: Isaiah 65:1-5
precepts.why:
This goes with Christ saying he came not for the righteous but for sinners. “I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not”. Like the disciples, we didn't wake up one day as kids searching for the Lord of heaven and earth. The word was introduced to us and woke us up.

“I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.” We are called African-Americans, Haitians, Jamaicans, Puerto Ricans. That is a nation not called by his name.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. We are that rebellious people, walking in Christianity and Islam, our people following their own thoughts in these religions. “A people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face; that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick”: the churches and mosques. Then: “which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels”. You know that's the church: there was always a swine fest at the end, pig feet and all of that; possum soup, turtle soup.

“Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou.” That is what the churches say to the Israelites on the street preaching: stand by yourself, I don't need no black Jesus, I'm washed in the blood of Jesus, I'm water baptized, I'm holier than thou. “These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.” God can't stand them.

That is the people Jeremiah calls an Outcast, “This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.” Those who think they are whole push away the physician; the sick who admit it are the ones he heals.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:24
precepts.why:
How does the Lord restore health unto us? “Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.”

Christ bare our sins in his own body on the tree, which is the cross; the cross was made from a tree. We, being dead to sin, should live unto righteousness. We are healed by Christ's punishment, his crucifixion.

That is the prophecy of Jeremiah 30:17: “For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. How? When he sent Christ to die on the cross. By his stripes we are healed.

Then: “because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”. Outcast means African-American: made-up names they gave our race. Nobody gives a damn about you, blacks and Latinos; no man seeks after you. But the Lord does. The wound no medicine could close is healed by his stripes, and then “all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: every one of them, not some.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:18-24
thread.text: Thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces; and the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.

precepts.label: Numbers 1:52
precepts.why:
Just before this, the Lord says, “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”, and that healing came when he sent Christ to die on the cross: by his stripes we are healed. “because they called thee an Outcast”: outcast means African-American, made-up names for our race, a Zion “whom no man seeketh after”. Nobody gives a damn about blacks and Latinos. Then: “Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents”.

What are Jacob’s tents? “And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, throughout their hosts.” Every man by his own camp: Judah is going to be with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim, Benjamin with Benjamin. That is the restructuring, the restoration of a nation.

And every man by his own standard: Judah had the standard of the lion, Benjamin the wolf, Naphtali the deer, Ephraim the bull. When the Lord brings again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, all of this is being restored again: the tribes set back in order, each under its own standard.

precepts.label: Numbers 24:5
precepts.why:
All of this is being restored again: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!”

The tents of Jacob, pitched every man by his own camp and his own standard, are goodly in the eyes of the Lord. These are the same tents Jeremiah speaks of when the Lord says, “I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces”.

So the promise of Jeremiah 30:18 is that the goodly order Israel had in the wilderness, the tribes camped in their tents, is brought back out of captivity. What was taken captive, the Lord returns, and Jacob’s tents are goodly again.

precepts.label: Psalms 78:55
precepts.why:
“He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.” He cast out the heathen before us, divided the land to the tribes by line, and set each tribe in its tents.

That is what it means for the Lord to bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents. The tents of Jacob are the tribes of Israel dwelling in their own inheritance, and to bring them again is to cast out the heathen once more and set the twelve tribes back in their inheritance.

Then Jeremiah goes on: “and the city shall be builded upon her own heap”, because that land is going to be destroyed and built again, and the tribes dwell in it again as the Lord made them to dwell at the first.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:10-13
precepts.why:
“the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.” It says heap because that land is going to be destroyed and built again; the palace means the temple that is going to be built. Isaiah 60 goes with Jeremiah 30:18.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” The strangers build the walls when Jerusalem is built again on her own heap.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. That is the palace. “and I will make the place of my feet glorious”: the Lord is going to make Jerusalem glorious again.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21-22
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.” That is why we go to Isaiah 60.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” Then: “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We shall not be small.

There is more in that verse than what it is saying on the surface. Look at the little bodies we have now. We are not going to have these little bodies. We are not going to be all frail and skinny, and the little fat brothers are not going to be like that either. The Lord multiplies and glorifies Israel, in number and in body.

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:25-26
precepts.why:
“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me”. The Lord is going to return it all back to the way it was.

Isaiah says the same: “And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:” “And I will restore thy judges as at the first”. He purges the dross out of Israel and restores the judges as at the first, the way it was in the beginning.

That is what Jeremiah 30:20 is saying: our children as aforetime, our congregation established before the Lord, everything returned to our glorious state. And it answers verse 21 too, “their nobles shall be of themselves”: our own judges, restored as at the first.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:7-8
precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” These are the same tents of Jacob that the Lord brings again out of captivity.

“In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”. The feeble Israelites are going to be like King David. “and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” The house of David is the 144,000; they shall be as God.

That is our children being as aforetime and our glorious state being restored: the Lord saving Judah’s tents first, and the weakest of Israel made as strong as David.

precepts.label: Psalms 72:4
precepts.why:
At the bottom of Jeremiah 30:20 the Lord says, “I will punish all that oppress them.” He said all, not some. All that have oppressed us shall be punished.

The precept is Psalms 72: “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.” Break in pieces the oppressor.

There is no coming together and joining with the oppressor. The Lord did not say he would reconcile Israel with the ones who oppressed them; he said, I am going to break them. That is the punishment of all that oppress us.

precepts.label: Matthew 2:6
precepts.why:
“And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”. Our nobles are going to come from our own people. We are not going to have nobles of another race, like the mayor they have now in New York, Mamdani. That is not our people.

Christ is our governor, and he came from the midst of us: “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” That is Christ right there.

So the governor that proceeds from the midst of Israel is Christ, born in Bethlehem of Judah, ruling his people Israel. “I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me”, and then, “ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

thread.label: Jeremiah 50:23
thread.text: How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!

classes.title: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:7
precepts.why:
“How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!” This Babylon is America, and the hammer of the whole earth is America, the oppressor. The same way the Lord used Nebuchadnezzar to judge Israel and all the nations, he uses America in these last days to beat all nations into subjection and bring judgment on them. America is no longer acting as Lucifer, the one about peace, justice and rights; it is turning back into who it really is, and it will oppress all nations, including Europe.

“Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand”. In whose hand? The Lord's. The Lord is the one using Babylon. Everything Babylon does, everything Trump is doing on the earth today, is because the Lord wants it done. “that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine”. That wine is oppression, affliction, falsehood, lies and deceit: the same cup the Lord told Jeremiah to make all nations drink.

“therefore the nations are mad.” Europe, China, Russia, Iran, the Arab nations, Venezuela: they are angry. America went into a sovereign country, took its leader, brought him back on drug charges and had four billion dollars' worth of oil shipped over. That is the cup, and Venezuela will not be the only one to drink it; even if they do not want to, the Lord will make them drink.

That is why the hammer will be greatly despised and broken. This is the beginning of sorrows; the world has changed and it is not going to get better. Prepare your mind and your spirit, and stop being caught up in sin.

thread.text: The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and my blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea, shall Jerusalem say.

classes.title: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.label: Zechariah 2:6
precepts.why:
“The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say”. The violence done to us, the Israelites, will be upon Babylon, and the Babylon here is America. But who is Zion, and where is Zion dwelling? Zechariah shows it is not just talking about the past, what Nebuchadnezzar did to us; it is talking about the future.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” The land of the north is America. Read on: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” And in Psalms 137 the daughter of Babylon is Edom. So Zion, the Israelites, is dwelling with white people in the land of the north, in America.

That means the violence in Jeremiah 51:35 is violence they will do to us in this land, and that blood will be upon them. Then: “Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee”. As we pray and ask him for vengeance and mercy, the Lord pleads our cause and takes vengeance on America for what they are doing to our people. So brothers, I know you are mad at what you see happening outside, but the Lord said he will take vengeance for us. “I will dry up her sea, and make her springs dry. And Babylon shall become heaps”: a burnt heap.

Until then, Zion must deliver herself: stop the porn, the fornication and adultery, stop worshipping the white image of Christ, stop carrying grudges, hatred and envy, serve God and get right.

thread.label: Jeremiah 51:46
thread.text: And lest your heart faint, and ye fear for the rumour that shall be heard in the land; a rumour shall both come one year, and after that in another year shall come a rumour, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.

classes.title: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.label: Matthew 24:6
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “And lest your heart faint, and ye fear for the rumour that shall be heard in the land”. What is the rumour we will hear in the land? Christ answers it: “And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars”. The rumour is war.

What kind of war? Not just rumours of war in Russia or the Middle East, but rumours of America having a civil war. “a rumour shall both come one year, and after that in another year shall come a rumour”: one year you will hear there might be a civil war in America, and another year you will hear it again. Then “violence in the land, ruler against ruler.” There will be violence here in the land of America, and they will not just fight each other; they will kill us in this land too, those of us who teach the gospel.

Read on: “Therefore, behold, the days come, that I will do judgment upon the graven images of Babylon”, the graven images of Christianity, “and all her slain shall fall in the midst of her.” That is civil war taking place here in Babylon. That did not happen to ancient Babylon, which fell by a coup, not by that violence.

So before that day, the Lord says, “My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord.” Deliver your soul: stop the porn, the fornication and adultery, stop worshipping the white image of Christ, stop carrying grudges, hatred and envy, serve God and get right, so your heart does not faint when the rumours come.

thread.text: As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.

thread.label: Ezekiel 20:32-38
thread.text: And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:15-16
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face. Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you”. This is our deliverance from Babylon: we go back into the wilderness, Christ deals with us and teaches us the laws again, and what he is doing to us there is purging.

So what kind of pleading is he going to be doing? Is it baby, baby, please? No. The pleading is killing and smiting, and Isaiah proves it: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh”. It's not a damn R&B song.

That is the same fury Ezekiel speaks of: “surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you”. As he pleaded with our fathers in the wilderness of Egypt, where the rebellious fell, he will plead with us, by fire and by the sword.

So even after the deliverance there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us, people that still need to get right, and they are going to get it; Christ is the one who will give it to them.

precepts.label: Joel 3:2
precepts.why:
The Lord pleads with the nations the same way he pleads with Israel. Joel says: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. No baby, baby, please for them either. He will kill them, for his people Israel.

The nations are judged “for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” The pleading in the valley of Jehoshaphat is the Lord's vengeance on the ones who scattered us.

So when Ezekiel says the Lord will plead with Israel face to face in the wilderness “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”, the word means the same thing it means for the nations: judgment, smiting and fire, not begging. He pleads for Israel against the nations, and he pleads with the rebels in Israel in the wilderness, and nobody should read either as the Lord asking nicely.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:12
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. What kind of purge is he going to be doing? Killing. Matthew shows it: “Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Does anybody not understand that?

The wheat is gathered into the garner, and the chaff is burned. That is the rebels who “shall not enter into the land of Israel”. Zechariah is still talking about the purge: “in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” And even the third that is left still has to be sifted, refined, made right, purged.

The Lord is not going to give the kingdom to wicked negroes. The kingdom will not be open to wicked negroes. To get the kingdom you have to go through this fire and get right; there is no other way. You can't keep doing what you do and think you are going to get the kingdom. It is impossible.

That is why we have to fight for this and help each other. If I see you weak and say nothing to you, that means I hate you. So if I tell you, bro, you have to fix that, and you say I hate you, shut your ass up; I am trying to save your life. We are so used to not taking correction from each other that it feels like hate, because everybody has coddled you, and you keep kicking the can down the street until you are back on the corner doing what you do. The fan is already in his hand.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11
precepts.why:
The fourth kingdom “shall be strong as iron”. It began with Rome, and America and Europe are the extension of Rome, the iron of the feet. Now Sirach: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Who is that iron? The fourth kingdom that rules the earth today, Europe and America, the white man.

Who is your enemy? In the 1950s you understood who your enemy was. In the 1800s you understood. Forty or fifty years ago you understood. God says never trust him. As iron rusts, the rust will always appear again, and that is his wickedness. Even though he said, we changed, we gave you civil rights, we are not oppressing you anymore, you see the wickedness coming back now, and they are taking it all back. His kingdom is made of iron, and that wickedness will always return.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. He acts like he loves black people and cares about them. Beware of that iron. “and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” If you are righteous and have wisdom, you see all his wickedness as in a looking glass: look at their history. They are a genocidal race of people, and you cannot get justice from them. Look at Palestine, Lebanon and the Congo, hundreds of thousands dead, while the ones running the courts don't stop it. This whole system is unjust.

That is why Daniel says the iron shall “mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”. After 1945 Britain opened itself to the people of its colonies, and after civil rights everybody started coming to America. The white man said he changed, and brought the same people he colonized and destroyed to live among him. Decades later they say they should never have let any of them in. The white man did not change; he is the same person, his rust has not been wiped away, and white people and everybody else are not going to get along.

precepts.label: Luke 11:17
precepts.why:
The fourth kingdom “shall be strong as iron” is Rome, and Europe and America are the extension of Rome. Strong as iron means strong militarily. But Daniel goes on: in the feet and toes, “part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron”. They have that same military strength Rome had, yet “the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.” Why broken? Because they are divided. That is what you see taking place right now: America is divided.

Christ said it: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.” A lot of times we use this for when we were divided in Jerusalem, and it is. But it is also speaking of the last days, of the kingdom that is set up in the last days, and it tells us what happens before its destruction.

Read on: “If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand?” Which kingdom is Satan's kingdom? Europe and America. America and Europe are divided; that alliance is falling apart. Here in America the citizens are divided. Satan is divided against himself, and that is a sign that they are about to fall. How can his kingdom stand? It can't.

The same division is prophesied of Egypt, and America is spiritually called Egypt: “I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” White people will be fighting white people, city against city, the same way the South fought against the North in the Civil War. The Lord is behind all of it.

So the iron kingdom of Daniel 2:40 is strong, but its own division is what brings it to desolation. The civil war things are already going on, even in the drawing of new districts between Texas and California to hold the House and the Senate. Pay attention: a house divided against a house falls.

precepts.label: Daniel 7:19-20
precepts.why:
Daniel asks to know “the truth of the fourth beast, which was diverse from all the others, exceeding dreadful, whose teeth were of iron, and his nails of brass”. The fourth beast is the fourth kingdom to rise up and rule the earth: it began with Rome, and Europe and America are the extension of Rome. The beast is Edom, the so-called white man.

“And of the ten horns that were in his head, and of the other which came up, and before whom three fell”. The ten horns are the Europeans; when the European Union was first formed it was ten nations, though today it is much more than that. The other horn that came up among them is America, and the three that fell before it are the powers America fought for its independence: France, Spain and Britain. This year America turns 250 years old.

“even of that horn that had eyes, and a mouth that spake very great things”. Look at the back of the dollar bill: the eye of a man set in the top of the pyramid, separated from the rest of it so it looks like a horn, with light illuminating all around it. It is not only the eye of Ra; they put the eyes of a man there. Those eyes are this man's wisdom and his technology, the wisdom Satan gave him. And it is his claim to be God: God sees everything everyone does, and the white man sets himself up as God and says, I see everything.

The great mouth speaks great things: he calls himself the people of God, calls himself a Jew, and says the land of Israel belongs to him. America has spoken many great things against God. And the great mouth is his power to communicate, to speak from one side of the world to the other.

“whose look was more stout than his fellows”: America is stronger than all the European nations. Why? Because of the technology, because of that great mouth and those eyes. Ezekiel shows the same wisdom in the prince of Tyrus, a rich ancient city on the coast of Lebanon that God uses as an analogy for America: “thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God”, “yet thou art a man, and not God”. “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”. With the technology we have, you can talk to someone on the other side of the world and see him on a device. There is no secret you can hide from the white man; every evil you do, everything you buy, he sees it.

“By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches”: that is how America became rich, through its technology and trade, the system that made the American dollar the dominant dollar in the world. But because he has set his heart “as the heart of God”, God says, “I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom”. That is future prophecy.

Daniel says “there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered”. What makes this tribulation different is World War III and Armageddon, and Psalm 91 shows how Israel is delivered in the midst of it.

“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” The secret place of the Most High is the Bible.

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The arrow that flieth by day is the missile, the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” And “he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. That is the deliverance of the Israelites in the midst of Armageddon: thy people delivered, every one found written in the book, not all nations. It is the same psalm Satan twisted when he told Christ to jump from the pinnacle of the temple.

precepts.why:
Daniel's “time of trouble, such as never was” is World War III and Armageddon. Ezra shows it: “And there shall be great fearfulness and trembling upon earth: and they that see the wrath shall be afraid, and trembling shall come upon them.”

“And then shall there come great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west. And strong winds shall arise from the east”: storms from all four winds.

They “shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star, Fire, and hail, and flying swords”. The horrible star is the ICBM, and the flying swords are the missiles. “And they shall break down the cities and walls, mountains and hills, trees of the wood, and grass of the meadows, and their corn.”

“And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid.” Babylon is America. And “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, just as Revelation 18 says the kings and merchants of the earth will bewail her. That is the time of trouble in which Daniel's people, every one written in the book, shall be delivered.

precepts.label: Luke 4:9-12
precepts.why:
Psalm 91 promises the deliverance of Israel in the time of trouble: “He shall give his angels charge over thee”. Satan used that same psalm on Christ: “And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence”.

“For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.” Satan twisted the psalm into a dare, telling Christ to jump.

“And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” Christ answered that way because the psalm is not a dare to test God. It is about the deliverance of Israel in the midst of Armageddon, when a thousand fall at our side and ten thousand at our right hand, and the angels bear us up.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:11-13
precepts.why:
Daniel says “at that time thy people shall be delivered”. John shows the order of it: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” That standing up is now.

“And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.” Between the standing up and the deliverance, John left out the tribulation, World War III and Armageddon; the precepts supply it. Tribulation has to come, then World War III, then Armageddon, when Christ comes in the midst of World War III.

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven.” A great destruction.

The Israelites who want to invest in airplanes and boats to get out do not believe the angels are coming. Come up hither is the deliverance: the angels bear us up, as Psalm 91 says.

precepts.label: Sirach 25:1
precepts.why:
“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” The Lord puts the unity of brethren first. Then the love of neighbours: the charity, the long-suffering.

Then “a man and a wife that agree together.” Agree on what? The commandments. That is not talking about arguing over the curtains. Brother, when did you become a fashion designer, an interior decorator? Let your wife handle that. The agreement God counts beautiful is agreement in keeping his law.

This is what the gathering of Zephaniah 2:1 has to look like. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: the nation hated upon the earth has to come together in the last days. But as we gather, we have to fix our character flaws, show ourselves friendly, and endeavor to keep the unity, and endeavor is an enduring word, not one to be taken lightly.

Unity of brethren does not mean you cannot correct one another or admonish one another. It means you expect highly of each other. We need correction, admonishment, counsel and advice amongst each other. Those who push you toward hard things, who tell you the harsh truth when a lie would be easier, are your people. That is how the gathered nation stands up beautiful before God and men.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” Love for one another means we are not supposed to suffer sin on one another.

So if I see my brother or my sister in the midst of sin, I might have to give them that rough talk. And it is to do what? To put them back in the righteous mindset. Real admonishment and love, being able to correct your brothers, comes with a little bit of hard criticism. You cannot take it emotionally, and you cannot take it personally. Tell the brother he is fat: fix it, brother. That is love, not hate.

Friends who roast each other are the loyal ones; those who value your success over the need to be liked are the ones who truly want your best. Their words are heavy, but their loyalty is pure. Don’t think that because a man is charitable he doesn’t correct anybody. We have to stop thinking with that emotional Christianity.

This is how the nation of Zephaniah 2:1 gathers. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: in the last days we gather with the believers who fear the Lord, and until we receive our homeland we are all we got. Rebuking one another in love keeps the gathered body clean and keeps the unity.

Zechariah says, “I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. In the day when things are going well, you forget what it was like to be in your lowest state, and you have to take heed lest you fall. If you would just purge your spirit, you would be able to receive all the things the Lord has promised for the future. But you quit because you forgot what the goal was; you forgot the mission, so you want to abandon ship.

When you are going through that adversity, be patient in your lowest state and don't forget the prosperity to come. That is what strengthens your faith through the refining, until the Lord says, “It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

We are nothing but humble servants of the Lord, working together in the vineyard. You are turning your back to the Master and saying, I don't want to do the work anymore. You have to walk through hell to get to heaven. There is no shortcut and no roundabout to the kingdom; you walk straight through. If you don't want to do it, don't do it.

So don't fear them that kill the body, because the things we teach will get us killed, and you will not deny Christ if you have not swallowed their crafty counsel.

“And ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” For whose name? For the black Messiah, not white Jesus. Everybody in the world loves white Jesus. But say Christ is black and look at the faces of the Christians. In their minds they are saying, we just want to get along.

Revelation 1 describes Christ with his head and his hairs like wool. Christ is a black man. He is a man of colour, and we cannot be ashamed to confess that.

That is why the nations hate us: for confessing the true Christ. And if you ever see a big white man passing in the sky, run; you are going back into captivity, because white Jesus will never show up. All nations saved would mean the other nations still ruling over you, with nothing changed. Your oppressor is the villain; do not join hands with him in these last days.

“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another”. Hold fast to the testimony of the black Messiah and do not be ashamed of it, even unto death.

thread.label: Matthew 24:4

classes.title: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:16
precepts.why:
Christ said “Take heed that no man deceive you”, and then: “ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.” Nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom, famines, pestilences and earthquakes: “All these are the beginning of sorrows.” That is the time we are living in right now: the beginning.

Ezra shows it is only the beginning: “For yet greater evils than those which thou hast seen happen shall be done hereafter.” Greater evils. The things you see taking place on the earth are only the beginning. It is not going to get better, and it is not going to go away. The Democrats are not going to come into office and change anything and make it better. God says it is the beginning of sorrows.

“For look how much the world shall be weaker through age, so much the more shall evils increase upon them that dwell therein.” The older the world gets, the weaker it becomes, and we are at the end of it right now. The evil is war, death and destruction, and it is going to increase.

So when you see these things, do not be troubled and worried about what is taking place. The world has changed and it is not going to be the same. Work on getting yourself right, and prepare for what is coming.

thread.label: Matthew 24:9-14
thread.text: Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:2
precepts.why:
“And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Why is iniquity going to abound? Because of the false prophets: the false Christians and these foolish Abrahamic religions teaching lie after lie. They glorify sin; sin is being glorified. And the love of many waxing cold means we are going to start to hate one another.

Ezra was told the same thing: “But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” The angel was telling Ezra that iniquity would go way beyond anything he had known or seen.

And look at it now. Men are cutting their privates off and having a vagina cut in there. That was unheard of. Women are getting penises sewn on. You cannot make this stuff up. Magic Johnson's son says he is only attracted to straight men; if he is attracted to you, he is not straight.

That is iniquity increased above anything heard of long ago, exactly as the angel said. So repent. “But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved”: we have to endure the hardships, the tribulation and the persecution Christ said would come, and not let our love wax cold.

precepts.label: Revelation 7:1-4
precepts.why:
“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Earlier Christ said in Matthew 10, “Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” So we are not going to reach all the Israelites. Then what does “all the world” mean, and when does the end come? Revelation 7 answers.

“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”. That is the fighting, the wars. “That the wind should not blow on the earth”: the armies. “Nor on the sea”: the marines and the navies. “Nor on any tree”: what is above the trees is the air force.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is not the hexagram. It is the law: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” He cried to the four angels “to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea”, hurt it with destruction: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

“And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” So the end begins when the 144,000 are sealed. The world Christ is talking about in Matthew 24 is the 144,000: when they are sealed, then shall the end come.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:5
precepts.why:
Revelation 7 has four angels holding the four winds of the earth. Let the Bible say what the wind is. Write it down: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”.

Where did the multitude come from? From the four winds of heaven. And what did they come for? To subdue the man that came out of the sea. So the winds are their armies coming against the Son of God, coming against the master.

That is why the four angels hold the winds so they do not blow on the earth, the sea or any tree: the armies on land, the navies and marines on the sea, and the air force above the trees. The destruction is held back until the servants of God are sealed. When the 144,000 are sealed, the winds are let go, the nations gather for war, and after that tribulation the Son of man comes in the clouds of heaven.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
In Revelation 7 another angel ascends from the east “having the seal of the living God”, and the destruction is held back “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” What is the seal of the living God?

It is not the hexagram. Many of us thought so years ago when we were young. Isaiah says what it is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal of the living God is the law, bound up and sealed among his disciples. Pay attention, because if you blink you might miss it.

So the servants sealed in their foreheads are the ones with the law of God in their minds: “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” When they are sealed, the four winds are loosed and the end comes. That is why this gospel, the law and the testimony, has to be preached in all the world for a witness: to seal the 144,000 before the end.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:19-21
precepts.why:
Remember, the 144,000 have to be sealed, and then the end comes. Isaiah shows what they do: “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”. Those that escape are the 144,000. He sends them “to Tarshish”, Spain; “Pul”, Libya; “and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal”, Turkey; “and Javan”, the Grecian islands; “to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory”.

There will be people who have not heard the fame of the Lord and have not seen his glory: Israelites who have not heard or seen anything, and we have to go get them. “And they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.” That is “this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations”.

You might think that is talking about now. The next verse clears it up: “And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem”. Jerusalem is already established as holy. Is Jerusalem holy today? No, there are bombs and missiles going off there. So this is not now; the kingdom is already set up.

“And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the Lord.” The brothers gathered from among those nations, the Lord will make them priests and Levites. With that, Matthew 24:14 gives a deeper understanding: the gospel preached in all the world is the work of the 144,000, and once they are sealed, the end comes.

thread.label: Matthew 24:29-31
thread.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:

precepts.label: Isaiah 34:4-5
precepts.why:
“Immediately after the tribulation of those days”: the churches argue about a seven-year dispensation, pre-trib and post-trib, and say the church is not going through tribulation. They do not know the Bible. Those who are alive must and will go through tribulation. Then “the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles, rockets. “And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: that is war. Notice it says heavens, plural; it is not talking about the sky. What powers of the heavens?

Isaiah shows it: “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”, the mushroom effect. “And all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree”: missiles and rockets falling.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”. Christ said his sword would be bathed in heaven, so what heaven is he going to bathe his sword in? “Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Idumea is the so-called white man, the leading race on the planet. The powers of the heavens shaken is the war with Idumea, all these Edomite nations.

So Christ comes back for war, not only to save. The order is tribulation, then war between the nations, then the sign of the Son of man. The gap may be five years, as World War II was once America entered, or seven; it does not say.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Who is the elect? Not everybody.

Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. We are the elect. Israel is the elect. Not the Baptist church, and not all races on the planet.

And it is from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other, because Isaiah 66 already showed there are Israelites scattered in the isles afar off who have not heard his fame nor seen his glory, and we have to go get them.

Before that gathering, “then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”. It is going to be a happy day, but we will be crying and fearful too. And it comes only after the tribulation. Christ is not returning this year or next year; bad things have to happen first and we have to be proven. Not being able to pay your light bill is not tribulation. We are too comfortable, still smoking weed, going to the club, defiling the Sabbath, the women dressed like hoes with no clothes; in their affliction they will seek him, and the affliction has not even begun.

precepts.label: Luke 21:25-28
precepts.why:
Luke tells the same coming, and shows where we are in it. “And there shall be signs in the sun”, like a solar eclipse, “and in the moon”, blood moons and lunar eclipses, “and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations”: we are seeing that now. “With perplexity”: perplexity means confusion. “The sea and the waves roaring”: the nations roaring.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” That is war. “And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” Right now we are in verse 25 going into the top part of verse 26.

“And when these things begin to come to pass”: the signs in the sun, the moon and the stars, the distress of nations with perplexity. “Then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” We are supposed to be looking up and lifting up our heads, knowing redemption is soon to come.

But we know the order of what is going to happen: tribulation, war, then Christ. So this is our time to clean ourselves up and get right with the Lord, because the time is drawing close.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:15-16
precepts.why:
When Christ comes after the tribulation and the war, he does not come only to gather; he comes to judge. Isaiah shows it: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.”

“For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” All flesh. The slain of the Lord shall be many, and that is not just Esau. The wicked Israelites too.

That is why Christ is not coming tomorrow to rapture a comfortable church out of trouble. He comes with fire and sword against the nations of Idumea, and against every wicked one, including our own people who keep smoking, clubbing, and defiling the Sabbath. The powers of the heavens are shaken, his sword is bathed in heaven, and only his elect, Jacob and Israel who repented and endured, are gathered from the four winds.

precepts.label: John 1:29
precepts.why:
At the Passover dinner Christ took the cup and said, “For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” The blood the Israelites put on the doorposts in ancient Egypt represented Christ's blood. It represented the new covenant: Christ coming and dying for our sins.

John shows who the lamb is: “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God”. Christ is called the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year represents Christ. He is that sacrifice.

So we do not sacrifice anymore, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today; some brothers are crazy. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God. Believing in Christ and doing what is right is what protects you from the wrath of God.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
The bread represents Christ's body, and the cup his blood “shed for many for the remission of sins.” Paul says it plainly: “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

Christ is our passover. The lamb that was killed represents Christ, and that is saying a lot. He was sacrificed for us; he came and died for our sins.

So you do not have to go kill a lamb and put the blood over the doorpost so that you do not die. You believe in Christ and you keep the commandments, and we come together, we break bread and we drink wine, as Christ did with the twelve at the Passover. That is being under the new covenant.

thread.text: And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?

thread.label: Mark 7:21-23
thread.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

precepts.label: Acts 5:1-3
precepts.why:
Christ said evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders and the rest come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “defile the man.” So how do those evil things get into your mind? Remember who the war is against: Satan. Acts shows how he does it.

“But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost” What did Satan do? He filled his heart to lie. That lying spirit comes from Satan.

That is how he works. He is there in your head, whispering thoughts, tempting you, putting things there that are not there. The deacon says something to you and Satan says, why did he say that to you? The deacon don't like you. A husband gives his wife an order to clean the bathroom, and Satan whispers: you going to let him talk to you like that, after all you do in this house? He don't understand you; he don't love you. If she listens, she becomes bitter and it shows in her actions.

Satan puts things in everyone's head, the deacon included. The fight with Satan starts first and foremost in your mind, and many fall in this truth because they wait until the mind is already defiled. To win, you have to kill it right there: the thoughts Satan puts in your mind should never become action. Ask, why am I thinking like this? Fast and pray, Lord take these thoughts out of my mind, and answer him with the word of God, “the sword of the Spirit”, the weapon we fight with.

thread.label: Mark 9:21-29
thread.text: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.

precepts.label: Genesis 30:2
precepts.why:
When Rachel wanted a child and came demanding one from Jacob, “Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?” Jacob could not give what only God gives. Go ask God for that baby.

That is the same answer for the single sister who points at leadership because she has been here five, six, seven years and has no lord, while a sister who came after her already has one. Leadership is not in God’s stead. If you want a lord, go ask God, and ask him what he wants you to change first. Check yourself: maybe talk to the sister who came after you and ask how she did it, instead of calling it hatred from leadership. God put leadership in your life to watch over your soul. Be the Proverbs 31 woman, fix your mouth, do the work on the body, stop eating the ice cream at night, and know your size before you point at the fit brother. It is not something you deserve; it is something you earn, by sacrifice.

The same dumb spirit Christ cast out of the boy tells that sister to go into the world, get a lord, and bring him in, when in the world she caught nothing before. Go into the world and you are still the same negro, still the same woman; you never changed, because you would not go to the Lord. Some came here for the ride and not the work. One sister reached out to a man in the world, and he is gone; another left for a man online who said he did not believe in two or three wives, then found out he did. Some of you are not going to get a lord in this captivity, and if that is what you came for, Satan will move you out of the way.

That spirit is the one that “ofttimes” cast the child “into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”: the paycheck spent in the club that gets sprayed up, the drunk drive that costs your limbs, the mob on Eastern Parkway, in the mix of a bunch of no-good negroes up to no good. Leaving your house to go with the dumb negroes is a dumb spirit. We thought it was cool; it was a dumb and deaf spirit, not listening and not seeing our condition. “If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth”: your belief is your power. When Satan keeps attacking you, your faith is weak, so cry like the father, “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.”

“This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.” Some demons are higher than others, so fast and pray, and do not let it conquer you. And once made whole, hear Christ: “sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” The world you left two years ago is not the world you would go back to; sin has multiplied, and worse demons are jumping on people.

precepts.label: Romans 8:28
precepts.why:
“But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.” Every hair on your head is numbered, so nothing can happen to you unless the Lord allows it. Don't be living and rolling in fear, and don't be scared of no damn ICE. A man's going is of the Lord. The spirit of Christ dwells in you; you are valuable.

Paul adds, “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God.” If you love God, whatever happens, even bad things in your life, happens for good. When Aquila and Priscilla were deported, it was for good: they ended up as Paul's helpers teaching the gospel. God had a plan for them.

“To them who are the called according to his purpose.” Every last one of us is called according to God's purpose. None of us knows where our going is or what the Lord has planned for us, but he has a purpose for each of us.

A brother in France was told to stop teaching the word of God or leave. He would not stop, so they labelled him an extremist, refused to renew his papers, and deported him. Right now he is in Ghana, doing good, all praises to the Lord. So don't think papers, a green card or citizenship will protect you; laws are being set up to take them away from those who speak against America or Christianity. If they take your green card and send you back, it is what it is, of the Lord. Don't run, don't cry and lose your dignity; make preparation, and go over there and teach the word, because all things work together for good to them that love God.

thread.label: John 3:6-8
thread.text: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:20-21
precepts.why:
“Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” Christ says “The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” What is that really saying? Isaiah shows it.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.” That word you hear, this is the way, walk ye in it, is how you are born. That is how you are born of the spirit.

The wind that blows where it will is the word of God. You don't know who the word of God is going to affect. The sound thereof is “This is the way, walk ye in it”, the word of God. Every last one of us in here heard the truth, heard that sound, heard that call, and it activated us. The Lord has his agents on the earth, like sleeper cells: you just hear a certain trigger word behind you and you activate, you wake up to this truth. The Bible is the activation.

And notice what comes with it: the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. A brother is born for adversity. When you are born into this truth and depart from evil, you make yourself a prey; Satan comes for you, and you will have to go through things. But the teachers are no longer hid in a corner, and the word behind you keeps you walking in the way.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:2
precepts.why:
Jeremiah cries, “Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.” As these times come to pass, we have to strive to be among each other and to separate ourselves from these other nations and from the unbelievers, because they will continue to come for us.

That lodging place is what the believers in Acts 2 had. “All that believed were together, and had all things common”, and they “sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need.” Nothing was lacking among them. They were on one accord, breaking bread from house to house, on one accord with their finances, making sure no one who was lacking was left in a constraint. “And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.”

What the Lord wants us to set up in these last days is a righteous underground railroad: looking out for the believers, the ones striving and getting themselves together. That means being selfless instead of selfish. It does not mean sell your last. It means that if you have excess, start consolidating, because this place is over.

Too many are still running up their credit cards and putting everything in debt, not realizing the tribulation that is coming. As the tribulation happens we have to align ourselves with what the Lord is telling us to do: come out from among the adulterers and treacherous men, and make a lodging place for the believers.

thread.label: Acts 14:22
thread.text: Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.

classes.title: Cyber Warfare: The Mouth Of The Beast

precepts.label: Micah 4:10
precepts.why:
Paul and Barnabas went about “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The tribulation hasn't fully started; you see it on a certain scale, but it will intensify. It will get worse, and worse, and worse.

Micah says how to go through it: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”. The Bible says to be in pain. Pain is coming, and it has already begun; pay attention to what Trump and these people are doing. But whatever pain you go through, you still have to labour, labouring in this truth.

“for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”. Where are we living today? Babylon: Mystery Babylon the Great, the United States of America.

Why does it say like a woman in travail? Because the pain comes and it goes, and when the baby is close to coming the pains increase and get worse and worse. That is what you see taking place now. Whether this society has another ten or twenty years, as the time draws nearer the pains will increase: the affliction rising against those of us that fear God. Keep labouring through them.

That is why the brother who is not studying and applying the scriptures has no root and will not survive it; when things get real he will be offended, scared, and go back into the world. Sisters, a brother who never teaches and is never in a camp video is a gamble.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
Much tribulation is coming, and Revelation shows where it comes from: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman”. The dragon is the beast, the white man, Esau. According to the prophecy they will be angry at us, “and went to make war with the remnant of her seed”.

Why? Not because we are evil or terrorists, but because we “keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The testimony of Jesus Christ is everything written in this book, everything the prophets said would happen, everything written about who the wicked are and all the evil the so-called white man is doing. That testimony says these people are the synagogue of Satan, and that God is bringing judgment on them for all their evil on the earth. As you teach it, they get angry and make war with us.

So do not think we will be out there teaching the Bible and everything will be good. The tribulation will be attacks from the government: labelling us a hate group, lying on us, putting us in prison, hitting your pocket and your food, attacking your wife and your children, because those are the things we care about. In the end they will force idol worship: worship the beast, or you can't buy, sell, work, get a job or go to the doctor.

The dragon is wroth, and he will make war with us. That is the much tribulation through which we must enter into the kingdom of God, and why we must be exhorted to continue in the faith.

precepts.label: Romans 16:3
precepts.why:
When Paul came to Corinth he “found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”. Rome commanded all the Israelites to leave. That is mass deportation, the same thing Claudius Caesar did back then that you see happening today with Trump and the ICE raids, and they are not raiding Europeans; they are going after the black and Hispanic communities.

But look what Aquila and Priscilla did after they were deported. They sailed with Paul into Syria, evangelizing and doing the work. When they heard Apollos, who only knew John, they “took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.” And Paul writes, “Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus: Who have for my life laid down their own necks”. That brother and his wife were not regular to Paul: they put their own heads on the chopping block for him.

Many like to suffer in silence, and the Lord is showing you your communication is weak. “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another.” When you are going through things, lean on the brothers; call and say I am struggling in this area. Out of pride we suffer in silence, get offended with everybody, and find ourselves out the door.

If he did not love us, he would cut us off, as he cut off Esau, whom he hates. You are supposed to go through it. Three flat tires? You have one more tire than you deserve. A whole kingdom is waiting on us, the world turned right side up, and we have to push through it manfully, together, or not at all.
