thread.label: James 1:14
thread.text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

precepts.label: Mark 7:21
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Lust has nothing to do with love, and love has nothing to do with lust; a lot of us get those two confused. What is a man’s own lust? Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.”

Read on: “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” Adultery and fornication are sins we battle every day. The spirit of murder you see in this world, and our people fight that demon every day. Covetousness we fight every day, because we lust and covet after these things. Deceit is a demon we fight every day.

These come from within. So the battle is not really from the outside; the thing we lust after is within us, and the battlefield is the mind. A brother can be quiet here but fighting major demons; a sister can be quiet but fighting demons. Quiet does not mean humble. Some are bound with their sin.

And this world feeds it. Everything here is a work of sin. They sell sex everywhere; you think you are watching a movie or a karate flick, and they put that nasty thing in there, and down the line you see how people turn to watching porn. The devil is always there, pushing sin. That is why we have to understand this walk and overcome it: every man is drawn away of his own lust, the evil that comes from within his heart.

thread.label: James 1:25
thread.text: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:8
precepts.why:
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10
precepts.why:
The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

thread.label: 1 Peter 5:8-10
thread.text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:

precepts.label: Sirach 42:24-25
precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another”. God created good, and he created evil also. He “hath made nothing imperfect”: Satan was not created imperfect. He was created to do exactly what he is doing, walking about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

“One thing establisheth the good or another”. What establishes the good of us and makes us perfect? When we go through temptation, when Satan attacks us and we overcome and are not devoured by him. Satan does devour some; some brothers and sisters get devoured. But those that are not devoured become better and become perfect. That is why Peter says “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect”. It is a hard saying, but without Satan, our adversary, we cannot become perfect, because it is his job and his children's job to try us, and as they try us they make us better. Even the real bad things: Job lost all his kids, and that was to make him perfect.

So learn how to fight him and how to see him when he is attacking. See him when he is coming, when he is trying to jump on you and put thoughts in your mind, and say, get out of my mind, Satan. Don't wait until he puts the thought there and you act on it, and afterward you are like Judas, what did I do? That is why the scripture says be vigilant: vigilant means you are watching.

And “who shall be filled with beholding his glory?” Those of us made perfect in trials and tribulation are the ones who will behold the Lord's glory.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:5
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That fire, the furnace of adversity, is temptation. Adversity comes from our adversary, and our adversary is that spiritual demon and his children. So the furnace of adversity in Sirach is the work of the adversary the devil in Peter.

Acceptable men are that gold. When an acceptable man goes through that fire, it doesn't destroy him. It makes him better; it purifies him. When Satan attacks and kills and puts in prison, some men it will destroy, and some men it will make perfect in the sight of God. When the ADL and all these governmental organizations attack us, some of you sisters will be up out of here: I ain't messing with them, the government say they a hate group. Some of you brothers will be gone too. But some of you will be purified and become that pure gold.

You have to go through adversity. Your enemy has to attack you; that is how you become better and how you become a better fighter. Then Peter's words come to pass: “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.” Nobody wants to suffer, but the Lord says if you want the kingdom you have to suffer, and if you are acceptable, after you suffer you will get the kingdom. Suffering makes you perfect, establishes you, strengthens you until you are battle hardened like somebody who has been warring for thirty or forty years, and settles you within your spirit: it is what it is.

precepts.label: Proverbs 30:20
precepts.why:
“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” If you love this place, the love of the Father is not in you. The state of mind of a saint is, I want to be up out of here; I hate this place. All that is in the world is “the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life”, and the lust of the eyes today is TikTok and social media, where the minds of a lot of young brothers and sisters are.

There is a challenge everybody is doing, a dance where they act like they are eating something. The song is called feeling on my body, and it is all about sex. Young brothers and sisters, even among us, watch it and mimic it, and some school sisters were doing that dumb, stupid dance on the new moon. When she says she loves an eater, you think she is talking about eating food? She ain't talking about eating food. She's talking about eating sausage.

The scripture shows what it is: “Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.” She eats and wipes her mouth, and then says she has done no wickedness. That is the characteristic of an adulterous, wicked woman, and that is what the dance is about: sucking rod.

So sisters, you should not be doing those dances. You don't even understand what's behind them. It is the lust of the eyes: you see it on social media and think it's cool. It isn't innocent; you are conjuring demons. We are supposed to be separate, not following the things we see in the world, because the world passeth away, and the lust thereof, “but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.”

precepts.label: Revelation 2:9
precepts.why:
John “bare record of the word of God, and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.” He saw things and he wrote them down. The testimony is what God gave the prophets: to Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Micah, Nahum, to Peter, Paul and the apostles. All the things these men wrote, the things that are going to happen to the children of Israel, is the testimony we as God’s witnesses are supposed to be speaking.

Here is one of those testimonies: “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”. The real Jews are in a low state today. Then: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

That is what you are supposed to testify about. You have to identify the people that say they are Jews and are not, and say plainly: these people are not the people of God. Revelation 3:9 says it again: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet.”

When you read Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 on this earth, that is you testifying. We as God’s witnesses have to testify these things on the earth today.

precepts.label: Malachi 1:4
precepts.why:
“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. Esau is going to rebuild. But “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. When the Lord comes back he is going to destroy all the cities Esau built. This is the testimony God gave Malachi, the same kind of record John bare.

“And they shall call them”: the “they” are the witnesses, the prophets. We are the ones that call them “The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

So the testimony is to let the Caucasian race know that God hates them forever. That is you testifying; that is the law and the testimony. The prophets wrote it, John bare record of it, and God’s witnesses on this earth today speak it.

thread.label: Revelation 2:9-11
thread.text: I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10-11
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”. They are going to pass laws to put us in prisons. That is why they keep building these detention facilities; they fill them with the people they call illegal aliens, but ultimately they are for the twelve tribes of Israel. Imagine ten days in a detention facility, being tortured, your wife and children or the brothers you war with slain in front of you, just to make you say you are not the twelve tribes and Christ is not black, and they will spare your life. Hell no. We have nothing to lose and everything to gain; they have no power over our souls.

Revelation 12 backs it up. We are going into Jacob’s trouble, when Esau does not want this gospel preached any further and will do whatever it takes to try to stop prophecy. “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.” Our kingdom is soon to come; before then, we are accused day and night. That is the tribulation ten days, us losing our lives for this gospel.

“And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony”. Their testimony is the testimony of this gospel. Even when persecution happens we will not fold; we don’t care about any white Jesus or any doctrine outside the twelve tribes of Israel being redeemed from our oppressors, Babylon America.

“And they loved not their lives unto the death.” We cannot be trying to spare our lives when Jacob’s trouble takes off. Loving not your life unto death means resisting every temptation to go against your God and your people. Don’t be a damn traitor. That is being faithful unto death for the crown of life.

precepts.label: Romans 12:1
precepts.why:
“Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” This is what we are going to sacrifice to get what is actually ours: eternal life, the kingdom of heaven.

Paul says it: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Every time these prophets go out to teach the word, they are presenting their bodies a living sacrifice. All the prophets in the Bible did it, even unto death. John was banished to the isle of Patmos; James was beheaded. They were martyred because they understood the mission, and you brothers and sisters have to understand the mission. We are the true martyrs.

Many read “be thou faithful unto death” and do not understand it. You have to put yourself there and say: there is nothing these nations can do to me, nothing you can take from me, to make me turn and betray my eternal life. There is no resurrection for them.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear”: you have to be spiritual, keeping the commandments, to understand it. “He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death”, the death the Lord has power over, the death over your soul.

thread.label: Revelation 2:10
thread.text: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a c

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-3
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. Did the literal devil come and cast people into prison? Did a spiritual demon snatch somebody and throw him in a cell? No. When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: it is talking about the father and his children. The same way we can do nothing without our Father and without the Lord in us, these people can do nothing without their father dwelling in them. He uses his children to do what he wants done.

Acts 12 shows who did it: “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.” Herod was a white man, an Edomite. He killed James and put Peter in prison. So at that time the devil casting into prison was Herod, Satan’s children, Rome.

The seed of the devil came back as Esau, and the sons of God came back as Jacob: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Satan means adversary, accuser, opponent: he is the Lord’s adversary and ours, and so is his seed. Devil means deceiver: as he deceived Eve, his children deceive everyone on the earth. That is why we call the so-called white man the devil, because he deceives the whole earth, and Satan, because he is our adversary and God’s.

So know who we are fighting. This is war, and the devil still casts some of us into prison through his children.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
Christ told the apostles, “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”, and he is telling us today these things are going to happen to us. How do we know? “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

You read the scripture say we are going to go to jail. You read that we are going to be afflicted, that tribulation is going to hit us. So wherever you find yourself, when these things happen you remember reading it, and you say, I cannot fight it, this is of the Lord. So you humble yourself to see what he is trying to show you.

That is why you cannot be a snake and think you are going to get away with it, selling your soul for nothing, for a little seventy dollars. The day you are sitting in the furnace of the fire, all of it comes back: the evil thoughts toward your brother, smiling in your brother's face while breaking bread, the things you did in secret against the congregation.

You have your own personal demonic sin you are fighting with. Get rid of that first before you think about lining a brother or a sister up for their failure. What was written aforetime was written so that when the trial comes, you have patience and hope, and you stand.

precepts.label: Psalms 140:4
precepts.why:
Christ said “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, and “be thou faithful unto death”. David shows who is working against us: “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

The purpose of the wicked is to overthrow your goings. You think Satan is sleeping? There is the spiritual Satan and the physical Satan, and every time they are at work, they are working as a team. He will get in your head while you sleep or get in your head while you are awake. At your job, Satan comes jumping into people, and you see people react some type of way.

This is war. That is why you must prepare your soul for the pain that is coming with their children, Esau's children. Whatever state you find yourself in, jail, about to be put to death, afflicted, tortured, losing an eye or an arm, be faithful, because pain is part of the walk. The body is not you; your soul is you.

Mark 9 shows how that spirit works in us: “ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”. That is us destroying ourselves in the club, the partying and religion, because Satan is in us and we thought it was the way. So pray to be kept from the hands of the wicked, and ask the Lord to strengthen your faith, because when your faith is weak, Satan keeps attacking you.

thread.label: Revelation 3:7-10
thread.text: And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;

precepts.label: Isaiah 57:1-2
precepts.why:
Philadelphia means brotherly love, and that church was a colony of Israelites. Christ, “he that hath the key of David”, tells them: “behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it”. That open door is salvation. “For thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.” They were under persecution, so he says he will make the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet.

Then verse 10: “Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world”. The hour of temptation is Jacob’s trouble, which leads into the world war and Armageddon. The church of Philadelphia will not be there when it happens. Does that mean a force field around them? No. They are at rest.

Isaiah 57 shows it: “The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” That is exactly what we just read in Revelation 3:10. “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.” Each one walking: they are not dead.

So when brothers and sisters die and people say, they keep dying, listen: I have a reason. They are at rest. You do your little tears and cry, that’s fine, but the Lord is keeping the righteous from the evil to come, the way he kept Philadelphia from the hour of temptation.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:2-3
precepts.why:
Isaiah 57 says the righteous “shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness”: they are not dead. Daniel 12 says the same thing.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. Those that sleep in the dust are the ones that died, and they shall awake, “some to everlasting life”: the righteous brothers and the righteous sisters; “and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

So the saints who died keeping the word of Christ’s patience are only sleeping. They were kept from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world, Jacob’s trouble, and they will awake to everlasting life. That is why we do not grieve the righteous the way the world does.

thread.label: Revelation 3:21
thread.text: To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:9
precepts.why:
“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame”. That is the business we are in: we have to overcome. With rank or without rank, a brother has to stay the same trooper. Don’t bail out now; it is time to stand up and face what we have to face.

What we have to overcome, Paul lays out: “Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” Your mother, your father, your aunt, if they are living an unrighteous life, will not inherit the kingdom. “Be not deceived”: not by Christianity, not by religion, not by the white man, not by the uncle or auntie telling you that you are in a cult. Satan can deceive you into leaving this life while you think you are still in the faith.

“Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind”. A lot of us are fighting the fornication spirit, the covetous spirit, the lustful demons. “Nor thieves”: some cannot stop stealing even in this truth, like the brother who borrowed the book and never brought it back. “Nor drunkards”: know your limit, because the drink spirit brings out whatever defilement is in your mind.

“And such were some of you.” That is the life we came from, so don’t think Satan won’t tempt you with these things now. And Galatians 6 warns: “if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work”. It is by the grace of God that you stand. When a brother or sister gets knocked out in this truth, your job is to fast and pray, never to applaud. Be your brother’s keeper; your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his. That is how we overcome.

thread.label: Revelation 7:9-17
thread.text: After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in thei

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number”. Now that we are bringing this out, the churches say we are all included, all backgrounds and cultures together. Where was that in 1964? Where was it on the slave ships? That is why the Bible says precept must be upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little.

Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. That is us. The multitude “which no man could number” is the children of Israel, whose number cannot be measured nor numbered.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people told they were not God’s people are the same ones called the sons of the living God.

It also shows time has gone by. Moses said “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”, because they were killing us; Hosea says we would grow to be like the sand of the sea. That is the great multitude standing before the throne.

precepts.label: Acts 2:5
precepts.why:
The great multitude is “of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues”, and the Christian says, see, we are all included. But read Acts 2:5: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

Out of every nation under heaven, and they were Jews. So “all nations” in Revelation 7:9 does not mean every race; it means the Israelites scattered into every nation, gathered out of them.

That is the all nations of Revelation 7:9: Jews out of every nation under heaven, the same people as the sand of the sea that cannot be numbered, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:10-12
precepts.why:
If you have time on the street, add Isaiah 11: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. Why the second time? Because the first time was under Moses.

He recovers the remnant “from Assyria”, modern-day Turkey, where you have the Afro-Turks; “and from Egypt”, lower Egypt and the Afro-Egyptians; “and from Pathros”, modern-day southern Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Iran and India, with the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits; “and from Shinar”, Iraq today and the Afro-Iraqis; “and from Hamath”, Syria today and the Afro-Syrians; “and from the islands of the sea”, like Cape Verde, the Hawaiian islands and the Melanesian islands.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” We are the outcasts of Israel.

That is the all nations right there: the remnant of Israel gathered out of every land they were scattered to, the great multitude of Revelation 7:9.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:38-42
precepts.why:

The number of thy children, whom thou longedst for, is fulfilled”. Verses 38 to 41 are Revelation 7:4.

precepts.label: Zechariah 4:11
precepts.why:
“What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof?” Zechariah asks again about “these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves.” The oil is understanding. The answer: “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.”

The two anointed ones are the two witnesses. In Zechariah’s time they were Joshua the priest and Zerubbabel. Before Babylon it was Isaiah and Jeremiah; in Revelation 11 it is Moses and Elijah. Different names, different people, but the same pattern: God always sends his prophets forth in twos before he brings forth judgment.

That is why Christ sent the twelve and the seventy elders out two by two. You cannot make judgment without two witnesses. And when the witnesses come they bind and loose things on earth, they forgive and they condemn, because it is the Lord speaking through them.

The two witnesses also speak of Israel as a whole. God says his people are his witnesses; and there are the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the northern and southern kingdom. A witness has a testimony, and Israel is sent to testify on this earth before the judgment comes.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:18
precepts.why:
“For thy help will I send my servants”: God says he is going to send Isaiah and Jeremiah. And that is what happened. Isaiah and Jeremiah came and prophesied before Babylon came and destroyed Jerusalem.

That is the pattern behind “I will give power unto my two witnesses.” God always sends forth witnesses before he brings forth judgment, and he sends them in twos. Isaiah and Jeremiah before Babylon; Joshua and Zerubbabel in Zechariah’s day; Moses and Elijah in Revelation 11. Christ sent the apostles and the seventy out in twos for the same reason: you need two witnesses to bring forth judgment.

So the two witnesses of Revelation 11 are the two major prophets that come before the end, and they also speak of Israel as a whole, the people God calls his witnesses on this earth. Judgment does not fall until the witnesses have prophesied.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:29
precepts.why:
What is the fire that proceeds out of the witnesses’ mouth? “Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” God’s word is like fire. That goes back to the same thing in Thessalonians: the wicked is consumed with the spirit of the Lord’s mouth.

So when “fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies”, it is the word of God coming out of the witnesses as they testify. As we teach the word of God, we are marking them for destruction, and every last one of our enemies is going to be destroyed with fire when Christ returns. “If any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed”: that is how they are going to die when Christ returns.

That is why Esau will try to kill the witnesses. He does not want judgment to come on him, and when the witnesses testify, judgment comes. As we teach his word, they are going to try to kill us, because they do not want us to testify.

The witnesses also “have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy”, to turn the waters to blood, “and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will.” As often as they prophesy, the earth is smitten with plagues.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
Read on in Revelation 11: “when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.” That beast is Edom. After we finish testifying the laws and the testimonies, everything the prophets say, revealing who Edom is and who the synagogue of Satan is, judging everybody on the earth, they are going to kill us because of our testimony.

Revelation 12:17 says the same: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The dragon is Edom. He makes war with those of us that keep the commandments and are teaching the word of God, the laws and the testimonies.

Revelation 18 shows where: “Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.” The apostles and prophets are here in America today, all twelve of them, teaching; and after they finish their testimony they will be killed. Before Babylon is destroyed most of them will be dead; the only one that might not be is John the Revelator. “And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.” Her is Babylon, America, and they kill the prophets here because the prophets testify against them.

The whole earth is our courtroom. The gospel has to be taught throughout the whole world and then the end comes, because we are testifying against everyone: to wake up our people that are scattered, and to condemn the wicked.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:4
precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. The “their” is the Israelites. Why does it call us dead bodies? Baruch 3:4 answers: “O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee”.

When we sin against God, God refers to us as dead. Remember the scripture says, keep my commandments and live. So Israelites living in sin are dead Israelites, even while they are walking around.

“And not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us.” That is why the plagues cleave unto us. One of those plagues is us going into slavery on ships: the transatlantic slave trade was a plague, one of the curses of Deuteronomy 28. Moses said we would go into tribulation again, this time by ships, and be sold to our enemies.

So the dead bodies lying in the street of the great city are the Israelites, spiritually dead, disconnected from our God, under the plagues that came because we did not hearken.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:10
precepts.why:
Baruch goes on: “How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land”? Now we are in our enemies’ land. America is your enemies’ land; they are the ones ruling this place.

“That thou art waxen old in a strange country”: we have waxed old in strange countries, because our land is the land of Israel.

“That thou art defiled with the dead”. What does it mean that we are defiled with the dead? We walk around like zombies. We have broken God’s laws and we are living in these lands not knowing who we are. We are confused; we call ourselves all kinds of different names and titles. We are the congregation of the dead, the valley of dry bones. That is us today.

That is why Revelation 11:8 says “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: the twelve tribes of Israel, spiritually dead, disconnected from God, lying in the streets of our enemies’ land.

precepts.label: Revelation 17:5
precepts.why:
The dead bodies lie “in the street of the great city”. Where is that great city? Revelation 17:5: “And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.”

That great city is Mystery Babylon, and Mystery Babylon is America: the greatest city on this earth, the greatest country on this earth.

And it is the great city “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”. The same spirit that was in Sodom and Gomorrah, the homosexuality, the lesbianism, all that filth, is the same spirit here in America. And the same spirit that was in ancient Egypt is here. Egypt means bondage, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. What happened to the Israelites in ancient Egypt, the oppression, has happened to them here in America, and is still happening. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 include the diseases of Egypt, because those curses were some of the same things that were on us in Egypt.

So the great city where the Israelites lie spiritually dead is Mystery Babylon, America, spiritual Sodom and spiritual Egypt, and this Passover points to our exodus out of her.

“The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened”: everything the prophets wrote, the testimony, is opened, meaning we are understanding it and teaching it. Then “the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues”, and received “seven golden vials full of the wrath of God”, and a great voice said, “Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.” The testimonies speak of the judgment and death that has to take place on the earth.

Amos reads: “Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?” That is the lion we read in Ezra, roaring and chasing the eagle out of the wood. “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?” The trumpet is the witnesses, us teaching; when we testify, the people better be afraid. “Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The Lord is behind it, through the angels with the seven last plagues.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The prophets are his witnesses, and the secret he reveals to them is his testimonies. And when he reveals it to us, we are supposed to testify.

“The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord God hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” The lion roaring is Christ speaking to us, and we prophesy. “Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt”: Ashdod is modern-day Tel Aviv in the land of Israel, and the land of Egypt is America. That is where we have to testify, and then the plagues are poured out.

Revelation 11:8 answers: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” That great city, spiritually Sodom and Egypt, is America.

So the great city was divided. Remember what Christ says: any kingdom divided against itself shall fall. Before God pours “the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath” on Babylon, something has to happen first: the great city is divided into three parts, “and the cities of the nations fell.” There will be civil war here first; then God is going to destroy this place.

The seat of the beast is America, and that darkness is not only sin, adultery and fornication. Ezra says, “the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The strait things are Jacob's trouble, persecution, great tribulation; the wide is the elder world, where Adam dwelt, the kingdom we hope to see on earth. “Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me.” The three shepherds are the scribes, the Pharisees and the Sadducees. Christ loathed them, and their soul hated him. “Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another.” When did we eat the flesh of one another? 70 AD.

“And I took my staff, even Beauty, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people. And it was broken in that day: and so the poor of the flock that waited upon me knew that it was the word of the Lord.” The poor of the flock are the disciples who followed Christ. He told them, when you see Jerusalem compassed with armies, run, and they fled. When it happened they said, that is what Christ was talking about.

The covenant with hell and death that our black and Latin brothers and sisters make with this white man will be broken the same way. It will not do them any good. precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
Ezra says the husbandman's seed perishes “if it come not up, and receive not thy rain in due season; or if there come too much rain, and corrupt it”. The husbandman is the Most High, the seed is the word he sows in us, and the rain is wisdom. Anyone who has planted knows that if too much rain falls on a seed, it does not grow. How can too much rain corrupt a man? Paul shows it: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.”

A novice is somebody new in this truth, a beginner. Some brothers come in and catch on real quick. Why would a novice get lifted up with pride? Because he got too much rain, too much wisdom, and he cannot handle it. He starts getting high-minded, and then he falls into the condemnation of the devil: Satan destroys the seed that is in him. That is what it means when the scripture says too much rain can corrupt the seed. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

That is why the heavy teaching is eased off at times. You may love it when the class goes deep, but too much of that wisdom too fast can corrupt you. The deacons have been learning in this truth for over twenty years. When you see them go into certain things, it comes from years of being watered; nobody woke up one day able to break down the scriptures.

So the Most High gives the rain in its season, moderately, as Joel says, “the former rain moderately”, raising the waters little by little, from the ankles to the knees, so that we can handle it. The seed that receives its rain in due season takes root and bears fruit; the novice who is lifted up with pride perishes like the corrupted seed.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:11
precepts.why:
Ezra sees “a roaring lion chased out of the wood”, and he “sent out a man's voice unto the eagle”. The eagle is Rome, and Europe and America are the extension of it. The roaring lion is Christ, but first it is us, the prophets: a man's voice speaking to the eagle. That is the witnesses on the earth today condemning the so-called white man, Edom, for all the evil he has done through the centuries. God has not forgotten slavery, Jim Crow, the destruction of Jerusalem by Rome. He does not forget anything.

How will we overcome that beast? “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome the beast, Edom, by the blood of Christ, and by the word of our testimony.

What is our testimony? The words of the prophets. We are teaching the laws and the words of the prophets, revealing that he has ruled with deceit, set himself up as the Jews and the people of God, and dwelt on this earth “with much wicked oppression”. In a court of law the witnesses must bring their testimony before judgment comes, and the whole earth is our courtroom. When we speak, the Lord is speaking through us, the spirit of his mouth.

And by the blood of the Lamb, meaning Christ having mercy on us. If you make a mistake, fix it. If you are struggling with things inside, fix it. If you fall, get back up; Christ will have mercy on you. But you also have to have his testimony. That is how we overcome this wicked society, and then the eagle, its horrible wings, wicked feathers, malicious heads and hurtful claws, will appear no more.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:9
precepts.why:
“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. Your body is a house; that is the house you live in. Set your life in order, brother, with God's laws, statutes and commandments, and then you can reprove and teach your people. And the Most High has set men over us to do that very work.

“And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.” Our leadership is wise, brothers and sisters; the Lord set them over us for a reason. They teach the people knowledge: how to overcome, how to lead ourselves in the way of righteousness.

Set in order many proverbs: that is what we do when we go over precepts. There are a lot of proverbs we read and don't understand, and leadership puts the puzzle together and sets them in order so you can understand the things of old. “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright”. They search out what the people need and what they are going through. Sometimes they step on toes, just to wake you up or break the chain you have been fighting with.

So God did not leave us without help. When we go off, he set up brothers and sisters to guide us back home. You can never say God did not send help; the one who ignores it is caught up in stupidity.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra to “comfort such of them as be in trouble”, and that comfort comes out of the scriptures: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That which was written was upright, and we have to understand it and follow it. That's the pattern.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. Don't let Satan take it away from you, and don't give it up for Babylon's money; Babylon will destroy your soul. Set your house in order, revive your own soul first, and then revive your people.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. That great multitude is what Christ said: you shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And “they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle”. Idle, i-d-l-e: a person avoiding work; lazy, indolent, slothful, workshy, shiftless, loafing; without purpose or effect, pointless.

In this truth, if you are idle you are avoiding work. Not work in the world: God's work. You are lazy in this truth. You have no purpose; you are just here. Some of you have been here for years and you have no office, doing nothing. You are idle.

“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Brothers and sisters, when you are idle in the truth, you are learning evil. That is why you spend your time on porn, smoking cigarettes, smoking weed, hitting women up in their DMs. You have idle time, and there is a whole lot of work in this truth to be done.

We can spot that idleness as soon as you come in: the one who sits down and just looks around, looking at the women's side, taking no notes. If this means something to you, you are engulfed in it; you are writing things down and trying to put it to memory. The idle are the certain ones the multitude will take away and feed.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1-5
precepts.why:
The idle will be fed “with things offered unto idols.” Idols in the Bible are statues, figurines, golden calves, and also money, career and power that compete with God for worship. So what is the most idolatrous religion here in America? Christianity. You may think that is biased; Paul identifies the religion.

“Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”. This is the latter times. Why will some give heed to seducing spirits? Because you are idle; you have idle time. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: I believe in God, but I am not going to do anything the Bible says. “having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry”: what religion forbids men to marry? Catholics; that is Christianity. “and commanding to abstain from meats”: who cannot eat meat for 40 days? Catholics; they call it Lent.

Those meats “God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and the truth is God's law. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Where is the food sanctified by the word of God? Leviticus 11.

The Roman Catholic Church is the mother church of every Protestant denomination on the tree: Orthodox, Jehovah's Witness, Presbyterian, Lutheran, Methodist, Episcopalian, Mormon, Evangelical, Pentecostal, Baptist, Adventist, Anglican, all the way to Christian nationalism. That is the idolatry the multitude will feed the idle, and they are already saying out loud that they are going to impose it on this country.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:6-8
precepts.why:
What do all those churches have in common? They worship the image of the beast. “And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” Their blasphemy is the perversion of the gospel of Christ, the perversion of the truth.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”. Esau made war with us: Rome, Spain, Portugal. Pope Nicholas V made that edict to enslave us and force us into Christianity. And they overcame us; they enslaved us. “and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.”

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: the same man that overcame us. A book published in 1920, The Pillory, the Tale of the Borgia Pope, says it is an open secret that Cesare Borgia, son of Pope Alexander, posed for the image of Jesus. Salvatore, the savior: that is Cesare Borgia. Even Muslims will tell you that image is Jesus; ask a Buddhist and he will say the same. Everybody acknowledges it as Jesus the Christ.

All that worship him are those “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” That is the idol the multitude will feed to the idle.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
In every place and in the next cities there shall be “a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Revelation shows who is behind it: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

The dragon is wroth: our enemies see us and they are angry. That is why in France they already said, shut down IUIC; a black Jesus, the Israelites, that is anti-semitic, we cannot allow this to go on. And he went to make war with the remnant: that is physical war, not only spiritual. That is tribulation, Jacob's trouble, persecution against those who keep the commandments and the testimony of Jesus Christ.

Christ warned of the same: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” You say you would never consent to their religion, but a whip across your back will change some of you, and you will be compelled to blaspheme.

And those who consent will be had in derision. Nobody likes a traitor. Like the apes in Planet of the Apes who betrayed their own and wore the word donkey before they were killed, Esau will use you and get rid of you. The ones who keep the commandments and the testimony are the ones the dragon makes war with; that is why Christ said, if they persecute you in this city, flee to the next.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:71-78
thread.text: They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:41-50
precepts.why:
“They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” We read the book of Acts and think that could never happen again, but Paul himself said, “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” The prophecy says it is going to happen again, and it happened under the Greeks too.

“Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king. Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” That is what is going to happen again. It happened in the time of Paul, in the time of the Maccabees, in Babylon when they tried to get us to worship the false god. That which has been is that which shall be; there is no new thing under the sun. Idolatry: leave that God and come worship this god.

They sent letters “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, profane the sabbaths and festival days, sacrifice swine's flesh, leave their children uncircumcised, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances. And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.” You think they cannot make a Sunday law and say, that Sabbath thing, no, worship God on the day we say?

The same thing we read in the Maccabees is what Rome, Spain and Portugal did to our people in the Inquisition; read Jews and Moors. And you say it can never happen, this is the United States of America? It happened during slavery. The same thing.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:34
precepts.why:
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” They did it in the time of Rome, when the Pharisees did it with Rome's guidance. Paul tells the Hebrews, “For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.”

Ye had compassion of me in my bonds: when Paul was in prison, they supported him. And they took joyfully the spoiling, the robbing, of their goods: their homes and houses, lands and properties. Those Israelites sacrificed their whole livelihood. They knew that supporting Paul would reveal them, and whatever they had would be taken.

Are we prepared for that? Do we really think about it? The cushy side of the room: I'm so comfortable, I got my new house, my new car, my new hair, my new nails. Are you ready for what the scriptures say is going to happen? Are we willing to lose everything, knowing we have in heaven a better and enduring substance? That is another level of faith we have to build ourselves up to in the short, limited time we have.

Even the world is warning that if a crisis comes and the government says get on a bus for your safety, do not get on: prepare your food, water, power and shelter so you do not have to rely on them. We have been telling our people that for years.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:32-33
precepts.why:
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” That verse is very important, because it goes back to what Christ said: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

Christ is talking about tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble. So what will the chosen be saying about Christ in that day, will they deny him or confess him? They are going to confess him.

Why does it say “Then shall they be known”? Because right now everybody says they believe in the Lord. Women say it; men say it. But when this starts to happen, you are going to see who is real and who is fake. On that day the ones who confess Christ before their tormentors are the ones known to be his chosen, tried as gold in the fire, and he will confess them before his Father.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1-6
precepts.why:
The chosen are “tried as the gold in the fire”, and Wisdom gives more detail. “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Christ said we will be afflicted, so what does no torment mean? That is the lake of fire. That torment will not touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” Christ said, fear not them which kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. Man cannot touch your soul. They seem to die because the body died, but the real man, the real woman, is not dead. We keep falling for Esau's craftiness: it's all over, we're finished. It is not over. They are in peace; that is sleep, rest.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. Jacob's trouble is just a little chastisement. “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us. Everybody says they believe; he will say, let that one get caught early and see what they do. He found them worthy because they confessed Christ before their tormentors.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is as a burnt offering to the Lord. Christ gave his life, and he said if you will not take up your cross and follow him, you are not worthy of him.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:38
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the righteous are tried as gold in the furnace and received as a burnt offering. Christ said, “And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.”

Christians say that means you cannot pay your bills and you have to carry all your problems on your back. No, that is not what it is talking about. When Christ was carrying the cross, where did it lead him? To death. He is saying the same thing for us.

We have to be willing to sacrifice ourselves. That is what Wisdom of Solomon was just saying: the souls of the righteous who die for the truth are in the hand of God. If you cannot confess the Lord, even unto death, you are not worthy to be his disciple. That is the cross, and that is how the chosen will be known.

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-15
precepts.why:
“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same. Be ye not afraid neither doubt”. Why neither doubt? Because doubt comes. My mama just got put to death, my children, my wife; Lord, are you going to save us? Remember John the Baptist when he was imprisoned; that little bit of doubt crept in. Acts shows the situation.

“Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)” James was beheaded; Peter was in prison. The angel brought Peter out, and he went to “the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.” That was a safe house where Israelites were hiding and praying. When the damsel knew Peter's voice, “they said unto her, Thou art mad”, and “Then said they, It is his angel.”

What did they think had happened to Peter? That he had been put to death. It shows you could not go visit him. There was no visitation, as there are prisons like Guantanamo Bay in Cuba today, with no lawyers and no visitors, and they are building more like it. So do not think, the brothers don't care about me, the sisters didn't come visit me. There will be places nobody can visit you. It is not that we do not care; we cannot get to you. All the saints could do was pray.

And Peter was on the run, a fugitive from the government the rest of his life. The Lord intervened for one and gave him more time, and the other, James, was killed. It is going to get like that, brothers and sisters. That is why we study, pray and apply: knowing ahead of time is supposed to strengthen your resolve, so that you are not afraid, neither doubt.

precepts.label: 1 John 1:8-10
precepts.why:
“for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down”. Why say, let not your sins weigh you down? Because we do sin, and churches love to try to trap you with it. “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.”

Christians on the street will say, do you sin, my brother? Yes. But my sin cannot justify you continuing in sin. Verse 9 is the key; verse 9 is the difference between me and you.

When we start cutting them up, they say, you think you're better than us? Do you sin? Tell them yes, and go right here and show them the difference. They are liars, because they teach that you can sin with no consequences. We teach that if we do sin, the black Messiah laid down his life, if we believe on him, so that we can fight to stop sinning. Simple answer; don't let them jam you up.

We do make errors and fall into folly at times. Confess it and keep fighting, and let not your sins weigh you down.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:11
precepts.why:
“let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”. When you keep entertaining that sin, eventually you will be bound by it. Peter says, “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”.

This is a spiritual war, a war for your soul. Take porn. Brothers say, I got it under control; it don't bother me. No, you don't have it under control. Picture a hallway of doors. A lot of you say, I only watch straight porn, like it is a good thing. That is door number one. Then the threesome, then the train. After a while you get desensitized; that does not excite you anymore, so you go to the next door down: chicks with dicks, then bestiality, then scat, then lesbian, then pedophilia. That is where the doors lead.

It is not normal. And you know it is the devil: when the Bishop was a little kid, his father had magazines hidden up in the drop ceiling. How did two little boys know to get a chair and climb up there, when they never saw their father do it? Playboy, Hustler, then VHS, then DVDs, and today easy access in your hand.

That is how iniquity lifts itself up until you are bound with your sins, covered like a field with thorns. Abstain from fleshly lusts; they are at war with your soul.

precepts.label: Romans 6:14-16
precepts.why:
When you keep entertaining a sin, it binds you. Paul says, “For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.” We are not under the law of sacrifice, but under grace. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.”

“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” His servants ye are to whom ye obey. If you wake up thinking about porn, go to work thinking about porn, and go to sleep thinking about porn, that is your god. You are its servant.

Grace is not a license to keep sinning; it is so that sin shall not have dominion over you. Christ laid down his life so we could fight to stop sinning, not so we could be bound in it. And when you are bound, there is no magic scripture that will release you; you have to want to be released.

precepts.label: Hebrews 6:4-8
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through! It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Hebrews says the same thing.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance”. Those who were once enlightened, who came into this truth, and fall away back into their sin or back into false religion: it is impossible to renew them again to repentance.

“For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.”

That is the field of 2 Esdras 16:78, covered with thorns, left undressed and cast into the fire. The ground that drinks in the word and brings forth fruit receives blessing; the one bound with its sins and bearing thorns ends in the fire.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:76
thread.text: And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.

precepts.label: Psalms 94:16
precepts.why:
The Lord God says, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” And: “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes.” Brothers give up their position because of the affliction, the little tribulation, or because of their bills, two hundred-some thousand dollars of debt. How could you be that stupid, that ignorant? We all have bills. That is all you have. Their sin is wearing them down so much, and they are so covered with it that they cannot see the brotherhood right in front of them.

David asks the question every one of us has to answer: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” You have to stand up.

The evildoers are where we are today. Taking a man out of his country and bringing him back to America: the same America that pushes democracy, when democracy put him there, kidnaps him and charges him with unjust judgment. Is that just, or wicked? If it is hard for you to see that America is evil, it is because you are evil yourself. Everything here is a work of iniquity; they push sin everywhere, even in a little karate flick.

Christ said, “I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world.” Have the word of God and the world will hate you, and your family will hate you. “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” He left us in the world because we have a path to go through: from Adam until now it has been good against evil, and our job is to stand for what is right. “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The stony ground “immediately receive it with gladness”, but has no root, and when affliction arises “immediately they are offended.” What have you given for this truth? Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are the children of Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you are alive, you still have it. So who will rise up and stand? Do not let your sins weigh you down.

thread.text: So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:7
precepts.why:
The brother about to die said, “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him.” It is good that this mortal body is slain when you look for a resurrection from the Almighty. “As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life”: as for the heathen, the fake Jews, the Iranians, the other nations, there is no resurrection for them. There is a difference between the twelve tribes of Israel and the other nations. The Most High made a covenant with our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Wisdom of Solomon goes along with it, and this has to be your mindset concerning salvation and gathering with your people: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of those who are against you come together.

So don’t get scared, y’all. Don’t be scared when you see your enemies’ blood being shed. Maybe some blood might splatter on you. Don’t get scared. The Lord has got our back, and we will not fear what man can do to us: you can kill this body, and we look to be raised again.

Until we receive our homeland, we are all we got. We are pilgrims here, with no favorite place, only our favorite people, the faithful brothers and sisters who keep the commandments. So we must keep the unity, show ourselves friendly, exhort each other, and show charity and mercy one to another.
